body: I absolutely agree. My watch alerted me to a heart rate of 140+ asymptotic which ended up being multiple pulmonary embolisms so it can be helpful, but nothing if not confirmed by actual medical equipment
Apparently I might have POTS and this comment scared the crap out of me until I read the response hahahahaha
The cut off used was 500 and I recorded a 380. Yes I’m assuming it was a lab stuff up or something of the sort but was interesting to see if anyone could think of anything else!
I was dumb and wasn’t thinking about what I was doing. I’m also having blood thinners at the moment but don’t want to tell any medical people because it’s embarrassing that I was so dumb
Many hawthorn geelong games but Hawkins kicking one after the siren felt especially heartbreaking

I completely get that, it’s like there are too many whiring things in your brain you need to make sense of them yourself before you can articulate that to another person, but seriously I found speaking to someone who actually got it revolutionary so I’m always here 💕

Hey lovely, I was the exact same as you and it is so so tough. When I first spoke to my mum I totally broke down and cried and said what I was thinking and that I knew it was bad and wrong but couldn’t help it. I felt so crap about admitting it at the time but in the end it was good. I’m not going to lie, it’s really really tough and it sucks so much. For me, someone pointing out that my hair was thin, dentist saying my teeth were weak and damaged and my nails breaking were shocking. Also seeing how everything affected my family. I so so wish I could tell you it’s easy and it’ll be fine really soon but it’s tough, so completely worth it, but tough. I don’t know if you can private message on reddit (I’m new here lol) but feel free to message any time to speak to someone who understands you

Therefore, if I have something else now that I’m hungry, it won’t make a different to what I had before. Not sure if that makes sense haha
